# opnsense_monit_settings (Resource)

Monit general settings (Services > Monit > Settings): polling, the alert mail server, the local web interface and M/Monit. This is a singleton that always exists, so it must be imported before Terraform manages it (`id = "monit_settings"`); destroying it only removes it from state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
import {
  to = opnsense_monit_settings.this
  id = "monit_settings"
}

# Turn Monit on and send alerts through the office relay.
resource "opnsense_monit_settings" "this" {
  enabled       = true
  interval      = 60
  mail_servers  = ["smtp.example.com"]
  mail_port     = 587
  mail_ssl      = true
  mail_username = "alerts@example.com"
  mail_password = var.smtp_password
}

variable "smtp_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable or disable monit. Unset keeps the current value.
- `event_queue_path` (String) The path to the eventqueue directory. The eventqueue holds alerts while the mail server is unreachable; empty disables it. Unset keeps the current value.
- `event_queue_slots` (Number) The number of eventqueue slots. Only used when `event_queue_path` is set. Unset keeps the current value.
- `httpd_allow` (Set of String) The `username:password` or host/network etc. for accessing the Monit httpd service. See [Monit Authentication](https://mmonit.com/monit/documentation/monit.html#Authentication). Unset keeps the current value.
- `httpd_enabled` (Boolean) Start the Monit httpd service. Needed for the Monit status page and M/Monit; requires `httpd_password`. Unset keeps the current value.
- `httpd_password` (String, Sensitive) Password for the Monit httpd service. Required when `httpd_enabled` is `true`. Unset keeps the current value.
- `httpd_port` (Number) Port of the Monit httpd service, from `1` to `65535`. Unset keeps the current value.
- `httpd_username` (String) Username for the Monit httpd service. Unset keeps the current value.
- `interval` (Number) Polling interval in seconds. From `1` to `3600`. Unset keeps the current value.
- `log_file` (String) The log file of the Monit process. This can be the keyword `syslog` or the path to a file. Empty logs to syslog. Unset keeps the current value.
- `mail_password` (String, Sensitive) The password for mail server authentication. Unset keeps the current value.
- `mail_port` (Number) The port of the mail server. Typically `465` for SSL or `25` for TLS and non secure connections. Unset keeps the current value.
- `mail_servers` (Set of String) List of SMTP servers for alert delivery. Hostnames or IP addresses. Unset keeps the current value.
- `mail_ssl` (Boolean) Enable encryption for mail server communication. Unset keeps the current value.
- `mail_ssl_verify` (Boolean) Enable or disable SSL server certificate verification. Unset keeps the current value.
- `mail_ssl_version` (String) Set the SSL version to use. In `auto` mode, only TLS is used. One of `auto`, `tlsv1`, `tlsv11`, `tlsv12` or `tlsv13`. Unset keeps the current value.
- `mail_username` (String) The username for mail server authentication. Unset keeps the current value.
- `mmonit_register_credentials` (Boolean) Automatically register in M/Monit by sending Monit credentials (see `httpd_allow`). Unset keeps the current value.
- `mmonit_timeout` (Number) M/Monit timeout in seconds, from `1` to `86400`. Unset keeps the current value.
- `mmonit_url` (String) The M/Monit URL, e.g. `https://user:pass@192.168.1.10:8443/collector`. If you want to control Monit services from your M/Monit instance you have to configure the Monit Port too and add corresponding firewall rules as well. Empty disables reporting. Unset keeps the current value.
- `start_delay` (Number) On system boot wait before Monit starts checking services. Seconds, from `0` to `86400`. Unset keeps the current value.
- `state_file` (String) The state file of the Monit process. An absolute path; empty uses Monit's default. Unset keeps the current value.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `monit_settings`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The singleton always has this ID
terraform import opnsense_monit_settings.this monit_settings
```
